value.rationale: The Tinkerbell map is a canonical quadratic chaotic map with a rigorously established chaotic regime and a literature on noisy reconstruction and invariant-state geometry. Because its nonlinear part is the real and imaginary decomposition of a complex square, stationarity links the first moment directly to the harmonic second moment. The accepted theorem turns that observation into a complete covariance statement: the barycenter fixes the covariance eigenvalue gap and principal anisotropy, leaving only total variance free. The centered specialization is especially rigid—exact covariance isotropy despite asymmetric linear parameters—and provides a simple exact consistency test for computed periodic or chaotic invariant-state statistics.
